# `core/gpu/DynamicUniformBuffer.js`

> **Source:** `engine/core/gpu/DynamicUniformBuffer.js`

DynamicUniformBuffer.js - Self-sizing uniform buffer from WGSL struct Pass in your WGSL struct definition (the same string embedded in your shader) and this class handles: - Parsing field names, types, and byte offsets (with correct WGSL alignment) - Creating the GPU buffer at exactly the right size - Typed CPU-side Float32Array + Uint32Array views - Named setters: buf.set('sunDir', [0.2, -1.0, 0.1]) - Bulk setter: buf.setAll({ viewProj: mat, cameraPos: [x,y,z] }) - Single upload() call to push to GPU Usage: const frame = new DynamicUniformBuffer(device, `struct FrameUniforms { viewProj: mat4x4<f32>, cameraPos: vec3<f32>, time: f32, sunDir: vec3<f32>, sunIntensity: f32, }`, 'MyFrame'); frame.set('viewProj', viewProjMatrix); frame.set('cameraPos', [x, y, z]); frame.set('sunDir', lightManager.sunDirection); frame.set('sunIntensity', 1.85); frame.upload(); // Or bulk: frame.setAll({ viewProj: mat, cameraPos: pos, sunDir: dir, sunIntensity: 1.0 }); frame.upload(); // Use in bind group: { binding: 0, resource: { buffer: frame.buffer } }

| `set` | `set(name, value)` | Set a single field by name. Accepts scalars, arrays, or Float32Array. buf.set('viewProj', float32x16); buf.set('cameraPos', [x, y, z]); buf.set('time', 1.5); buf.set('flags', 3);          // u32 |
| `setAll` | `setAll(obj)` | Set multiple fields at once. buf.setAll({ viewProj: matrix, cameraPos: [x, y, z], time: elapsed, }); |
| `upload` | `upload()` | Upload CPU data to GPU. Call once per frame after all sets. |
| `offsetOf` | `offsetOf(name)` | Get the byte offset for a field (useful for partial writes). |
| `floatIndexOf` | `floatIndexOf(name)` | Get the float index for a field. |
| `has` | `has(name)` | Check if a field exists in the layout. |
| `fields` | `get fields()` | Get current field names. |
| `bindEntry` | `bindEntry(binding = 0)` | Convenience: create a bind group entry for this buffer. entries: [frame.bindEntry(0)] |
| `destroy` | `destroy()` | Destroy GPU buffer. |

## Notes & Examples

### Shared GPU device

Engine subsystems should reuse the cached `GpuDevice` wrapper returned by `getGpuDevice()`. The wrapper owns the native `GPUDevice`, its queue, granted features, limits, and device-loss callbacks. Resources created by one native device cannot be used by another, so pass the shared wrapper or native device into each subsystem that needs GPU access.

**Example: Acquire the shared engine device**
```js
import { getGpuDevice } from '/engine/core/gpu/GpuDevice.js';

const gpu = await getGpuDevice({
  label: 'MyEngineApp',
  adapterOptions: { powerPreference: 'high-performance' },
  requiredFeatures: []
});

const device = gpu.getDevice();
const queue = gpu.getQueue();
```

Request a feature only when the application cannot run without it. `GpuDevice.create()` automatically requests the engine's supported optional feature set, while `gpu.getCapabilities().features` reports the features actually granted to the device.

**Feature and limit checks**
```js
const { features, limits } = gpu.getCapabilities();

if (features.has('timestamp-query')) {
  console.info('GPU timestamp queries are available');
}

const requestedBytes = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
if (requestedBytes > limits.maxBufferSize) {
  throw new RangeError('Requested buffer exceeds maxBufferSize');
}
```

**Device loss**
```js
gpu.onDeviceLost((info) => {
  console.error('WebGPU device lost:', info.reason, info.message);
  // Stop work and re-bootstrap the application so every GPU resource is rebuilt.
});
```

**Gotchas:**
- **First acquisition defines requirements:** `getGpuDevice()` caches the wrapper. Supply mandatory features and limits on the first call.
- **Native access:** use `gpu.getDevice()` and `gpu.getQueue()` when a subsystem needs WebGPU primitives.
- **Recovery:** this module reports device loss but does not expose an in-place `recreate()` API. Re-bootstrap all device-owned resources together.
- **Limits:** check the granted `gpu.getCapabilities().limits` before large allocations.

(Source: `engine/core/gpu/GpuDevice.js`)
